blind.why: Spectated FP tag at 25 m (spS_001, Sable's Judge vs Sprig) vs CS2 t1_020 (M4 kill at about 20 m). CS2's red mist on the target reads instantly in the world. In ours the hit reads mostly through the HUD hit-X and the crystal turning white. There is no visible line of fire. The muzzle flash floats in the air with no gun, and the muzzle light turns the near right wall into a flat, untextured yellow slab.

Third-party line of fire (spL_008, spectating Lumen in a 25 m duel) vs CS2 t2_029. CS2's long soft tracer plus a big hit mist tell you who shot whom. In ours the enemy's and the teammate's shots leave almost no trace. The most visible effects in the frame are a white blade-like shard and orange shard flecks on the floor, which read as glitches, not combat feedback.

Own pistol shot, local first person (fpB_009, 18 m) vs CS2 t1_019. This was the closest pair. Our own tracer is readable and leads the eye to the target with a small hit puff. CS2's soft fireball and the blood decal on the wall behind the enemy feel more grounded, and the hit is clearer. Our hard 8-point star flash still looks pasted onto the frame.

biggest_gap: The line of fire and hit confirmation are unreadable at 8-25 m in real fights whenever the viewer is not the shooter, including when spectating the shooter in first person. Repro: ?test=1&seed=1&match=1&phase=live with a local autopilot that dies at 10.0 s, then spectate Sable from 12.95 s (Sable tags Sprig at 25 m at 13.117 s and Blitz at 14.517 s) or Kestrel from 18.95 s (tags Sable at 7.8 m at 19.258 s). Shots: shots/critic-vfx-r4/spS_*, spK_*, zS2.png, zK.png. Sampled every 0.05-0.08 s, no tracer from the spectated shooter is visible in any frame. Cause: tracer() decides own vs other from the distance to ctx.localActor's eye, not to the render camera (src/vfx/index.js ~line 257). While spectating, the dead local body is elsewhere, so the spectated player's own shots get the thin, 0.55x-dim, 2.6 m segment that dissolves before the target. Even correctly classified other/incoming tracers are near-invisible at 10-25 m (spL, spK: Mika's and Sable's shots show at most a 1-2 px white tick). The world-space hit effect on a body at 15-25 m is about 10 px, so the hit-X does all the work. CS2 shows a soft, readable tracer segment from third parties, and every body hit at 20 m gets a 40-80 px mist (t1_020, t2_029). Fix: classify own vs other against the camera/view actor. Give other and incoming tracers a distance-compensated minimum of about 2 px core and 60-70% alpha, and keep them visible up to the hit point. Scale the body-hit puff with distance so it is at least about 30-40 px at 20 m.
other_gaps: Tag-out mesh shards are not faded or shrunk near the camera. Spectating Lumen 1-2 m from Blitz's shatter (seed 1, 15.25-15.5 s, spL_000-005) shows flat, untextured orange, white and brown triangles 40-120 px wide tumbling across the view in the middle of a live 25 m duel. They obstruct the view and read as rendering glitches. Apply the same near-camera shrink/fade the particle flecks already get.

Muzzle point light flattens nearby geometry. In spS_001 the right wall about 1 m away jumps from shaded brown to a uniform saturated yellow for one frame, losing all texture and shading. Clamp the intensity or range of the muzzle light near the camera, or lower it for the view actor.

Tag-out at 25 m: the crystal freeze reads well (white figure). The shatter is a faint pink ring about 2 m wide for 2 frames, and the 5-9 s glitter is a few 1-2 px dots, so it is invisible at 25 m (zS3.png). Nothing marks the spot the way CS2's lasting splatter does (t2_008).

Impacts on cover at 15-18 m are tiny. Pistol hits on the brick planter (fpB_003-005) leave a barely visible reddish smudge and a 2-3 px fleck, with no dust or chip burst that would tell you the shot was blocked by cover.
The FP muzzle flash is still a hard 8-point star with straight spikes. It reads as a sticker, not a fireball (fpB_002, fpB_005, fpB_009). The tracer leaving it is pale cream, washed out by the flash.

Cross-piece (not vfx-owned, but it ruins vfx readability): the spectator view has no viewmodel, so the vfx flash floats in mid-air (spS_001, spS_018). On local death the camera cuts to the killer within 0.05 s (fpB_010 -> fpB_011), so the victim never sees the incoming tracer or their own tag-out. With ai.debug.adoptLocal + spectate(Blitz), a flat orange slab fills 60% of the screen (fpA_*).
bugs: vfx tracer(): own vs other is decided by ctx.localActor's eye, not the camera, so in spectator first person the spectated player's own shots are drawn as dim, thin third-party segments that dissolve 2 m before the hit (src/vfx/index.js ~257-259; spS_*, spK_*).
Shatter mesh shards have no near-camera fade or shrink: huge flat untextured polygons cross the view of a teammate nearby (spL_000-005, seed 1, spectating Lumen 15.25-15.5 s).
The muzzle point light washes the near wall to a flat, unshaded colour for a frame (spS_001).
strengths: No console errors across 6 real-match captures. vfx draw-call overhead is small: total scene calls stay at 95-118 during fights, and at most about 160 particles are alive.
The local player's own tracer is now a readable, single, travelling streak (fpB_002, fpB_009), and teammate beams no longer flood the screen.
The tag-out crystal freeze is readable at 8 m and still at 25 m.
Landing and footstep dust is subtle and causes no clutter in first person (jmp_*). Bullet-hole decals are small and no longer smudgy.
